maya: Ran an nsys + perfetto trace on a 8xA100 cluster during the midday traffic run. Seeing repeating ~5-7ms host->GPU queue gaps at the tails of continuous-batch windows. trace id run-2026-03-05-1, perfetto link: https://perfetto.example/r/run-2026-03-05-1

maya: Command used:```nsys profile -o run-2026-03-05-1 --trace=cuda,cublas,cuda_memory python -m redwood.serve.trace_test```

maya: TL;DR: spikes correlate with KV cache sweep markers (kv_sweep_start / kv_sweep_end). CPU looks busy, but GPU compute stalls waiting for kernels to be queued. Suspect kernel selection switch + stream contention.

sam: can you paste a short kernel timeline snippet from the perfetto view? curious if it's kernel dispatch latency or memcpy scheduling.

chen: perfetto shows:
```
[11:22:10.123] kv_sweep_start (CPU)
[11:22:10.128] attn_fwd_kernel(0) queued
[11:22:10.134] attn_fwd_kernel(0) start -> 1.2ms
[11:22:10.140] kv_sweep_end (CPU)
[11:22:10.147] matmul_fallback_kernel queued
[11:22:10.153] matmul_fallback_kernel start -> 3.8ms (longer than expected)
```

chen: pattern repeats every ~40ms in long waves, but our batch_window is 15ms. Looks like periodic sweeps push some kernels onto a different stream or cause kernel selection to prefer a slower code path.

maya: grep from runtime log: `grep -n "kv_sweep" runtime.log | tail -n 5` ->
```
11023: INFO kv_sweep_start seq=all id=42
11023: DEBUG kernel_choice attn->fused_matmul reason=heuristic_seq_len
11023: INFO kv_sweep_end elapsed_ms=8
```

olivia: @maya what's incoming QPS during the run? could be batching backlog causing long GPU queues.

maya: ~1200 rps, batching config: continuous=true, batch_window_ms=15, max_batch_tokens=16384. Effective observed batch latency sometimes jumps to ~55-70ms when the kv sweep hits mid-window.

sam: that matches a scheduling issue: KV sweep runs on CPU and triggers kernel_choice change (we saw a fallback to matmul for some attention widths). Kernel change + running on a different stream can add enqueue latency for following kernels. Two proposals: 1) mark kv_sweep markers as low-priority so they don't preempt batch enqueue path; 2) ensure kernel selection decisions are warmed ahead of time (cache kernel_choice per seq_len bucket).

chen: I also noticed host CPU scheduling jitter right before sweep_start (htop showed short spikes from housekeeping). Could be a GC/py thread doing work. We should correlate with system metrics (irq, context-switch).

infra-bot: trace-processor: finished parsing run-2026-03-05-1. Extracted 482 kernels, avg enqueue-latency=0.9ms, 95p=4.9ms, tail spikes aligned with kv_sweep events (p<0.001). Trace artifact: s3://redwood-traces/run-2026-03-05-1.nsight

olivia: Can we repro with a synthetic load that forces regular KV sweeps? If yes, we can iterate on two fixes: kernel-affinity pinning or sweep offloading to a dedicated helper thread.

maya: I'll spin up a synthetic run that triggers kv_sweep every 50ms and collect nsys + perfetto. Will also dump kernel_choice logs with `--verbose-kernel-chooser`.

sam: I opened a short RFC/PR: "treat kv_sweep as maintenance op: deprioritize enqueue path" (link: https://git.redwood/pr/445). Plan: measure before/after on same infra.

chen: action items:
- maya: repro trace with synthetic workload + verbose kernel logs (due EOD)
- sam: add a patch to deprioritize sweeps and add unit test for kernel-choice caching (WIP)
- olivia: schedule infra-run on staging GPUs (2xA100) and capture perf counters (pmu + nsys)

maya: quick note: when we forced kernel-affinity=prefer-fused the enqueue latency 95p dropped to ~2.1ms in a local test. Not a production knob but useful datapoint.

sam: good. Let's avoid hasty global defaults; aim for heuristic: if kv_sweep detected inside batch_window, postpone sweep end work until batch completion or move to low-prio thread.

maya: I'll post the perfetto link + raw nsys output once the synthetic run finishes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
